name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
nameVi: Lăng Chủ tịch Hồ Chí Minh
kicker: A morning visit on Ba Dinh Square
summary: Join the morning line at 17 Ngoc Ha for the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the columned hall at the head of Ba Dinh Square. Visits run only in the morning and never on Mondays or Fridays, with a few named exceptions, and the building shuts for maintenance in the autumn. The citadel and One Pillar Pagoda fill the rest of the morning.
fee: Free (operator FAQ); 40,000 VND on Vietnam Tourism
heroCaption: The facade of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
gettingThere: Visitors assemble at 17 Ngoc Ha, in Ba Dinh, west of the lake. This is a different entrance from the Imperial Citadel at 19c Hoang Dieu. Take a car or motorbike from Hoan Kiem.

legs.heading: From Hoan Kiem
legs.body: By car or motorbike to 17 Ngoc Ha.

hours: Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun mornings. 1 Apr–31 Oct: weekdays 7:30–10:30, weekends and holidays 7:30–11:00. 1 Nov–31 Mar: weekdays 8:00–11:00, weekends and holidays 8:00–11:30 (operator). Vietnam Tourism adds a 10:15 last entry.
closed: Monday and Friday, except 19 May, 2 September, and the first day of Tet. Closed 4 Sep–2 Nov 2026 for maintenance, reopening 3 Nov 2026 (government portal); a relic page gives about two months each October–November.
admissionNote: No ticket for the mausoleum or Ba Dinh Square (operator FAQ). Vietnam Tourism lists 40,000 VND.

notice.title: Closed 4 September to 2 November 2026
notice.body: The mausoleum shuts for maintenance from 4 September 2026 and reopens on 3 November 2026. It is also closed every Monday and Friday, except 19 May, 2 September, and the first day of Tet.

body: The mausoleum stands at the head of Ba Dinh Square, with the flag on its tall pole in front and lawns on either side. Visitors assemble at 17 Ngoc Ha, not at the citadel gate on Hoang Dieu. Walking the square itself needs no ticket.

Go early on a Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, or Sunday. From April to October the doors close at 10:30 on weekdays and 11:00 at weekends; from November to March, at 11:00 and 11:30. Arrive in the afternoon and you will find it shut.
The Imperial Citadel and One Pillar Pagoda are in the same district, with their own gates and tickets, so the rest of the Ba Dinh morning is close by.
